Discussed tuning (quantization, batch sizing, cache hit rates), VPC networking considerations, and next steps for on-site perf test and security review.
topics: Latency baseline vs Omni's current provider
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check in, well go over last week's benchmark sheet, any urgent changes before we start?
[00:12] Jordan (Customer - Eng Lead): No, were eager to see the 16k context numbers, curiosity on p95 more than p50.
[00:20] Priya (SE): Great, Ill pull up the sheet, link is in the chat -- benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/sheets/omni-bench-2026-06-02. Note these are cold-start disabled runs, steady state.
[00:30] Maya (CTO): Quick ask, please call out which runs are hosted vs dedicated, and whether were using KMS keys in the V P C tests.
[00:38] Priya: Yep, column A is hosted (Redwood API), column B is Redwood Dedicated (reserved G P U pool), column C is Omni baseline (current provider). KMS was not used in these particular hosted runs but we did a VPC variant for the Dedicated rows.
[00:52] Samir (SRE): I noticed the p95 on the baseline spikes a lot for >8k prompts, can you explain?
[01:00] Priya: Baseline provider is showing inefficient batching at scale in their reported runs; on our side we see continuous batching + better KV prefix cache hit rates which reduces token generation overhead. For example, for 8k prompt median token latency p50 we saw ~95ms on Redwood hosted, baseline ~160ms; p95 Redwood hosted ~220ms vs baseline ~380ms.
[01:25] Jordan: Those are big deltas. Are those with same model family?
[01:29] Priya: Same open-model family (we used the 70B variant baseline-compatible), weights are aligned, quantization differs slightly. Our default bench used fp16 on Dedicated, and mixed precision optimized kernels in hosted. We also ran an int8 candidate that reduced p50 by ~12% and p95 by ~9% in early tests.
[01:50] Alex: To be clear, the key levers we tuned were: batching window, max_batch_size, and KV cache TTL. We also picked kernels targeted to your typical sequence distribution you shared, which gave wins.
[02:05] Maya: Any instability observed when enabling int8? We had concerns about quality and hallucination risk.
[02:11] Priya: Quality checks were part of the runs — we ran the prompt suite you provided. Int8 showed a small delta on a couple of targeted eval prompts but within your acceptance band you gave on the kickoff (less than 2% change). We captured sample outputs in the sheet.
[02:26] Jordan: Can we get exact numbers on tokens/sec throughput?
[02:30] Priya: Sure — throughput for the host config: p50 tokens/sec ~3400 for 2k context runs, drop to ~2100 for 16k context due to KV management overhead. Baseline provider reported ~1800 tokens/sec on 16k. On Dedicated we hit ~4100 tokens/sec p50 for 2k and ~2700 for 16k with caching.
[02:55] Samir: What was the cache hit rate for the prefix cache?
[02:59] Priya: On the test traffic the effective prefix/K V cache hit was ~42% which is higher than baseline's reported ~18% because of our smarter prefix grouping. That explains a chunk of the throughput win.
[03:12] Alex: Also worth noting we did a sensitivity run on batch_size, smaller max_batch_size reduced p95 but increased cost per token. We left recommended config in the sheet (tab: recommended-tuning).
[03:25] Jordan: On the network side, in V P C tests did you see any added latency?
[03:30] Priya: VPC adds ~8-12ms one-way depending on region and path. Our dedicated nodes in your preferred region reduce cross-subnet traversal; overall p95 went up about 10-15ms vs hosted non-VPC. We can show detailed traces.
[03:45] Maya: Security — what about audit logs and KMS?
[03:48] Alex: Well share SOC2 and our audit logging doc. We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Dedicated and Private. We'll attach the KMS integration doc in follow up.
[03:59] Priya: For the on-prem / private deployment variant we ran a small bench on a proxy node and results were roughly parity with Dedicated after accounting for network. That aligns with our thesis that serving runtime + kernel selection gives most of the win.
[04:14] Jordan: Can you comment on variability during sustained bursts? We do a lot of spiky traffic.
[04:20] Priya: Yeah, we did burst runs — Redwood Dedicated with burst capacity kept p95 within 1.2x of baseline p95 even at 2x traffic. Hosted shows graceful degradation via routing to fallback model variants; baseline provider dropped throughput more sharply.
[04:38] Samir: Any licensing or data persistence concerns for the pilot? We need to know retention windows and logs access.
[04:44] Alex: Logs retention for the pilot can be configured; default is 30 days, enterprise add-on for longer retention. Access via our console with RBAC and audit logs — we'll send the security checklist.
[04:55] Jordan: About pricing, we want a dedicated short-term commit to compare production numbers.
[04:59] Alex: Understood — we can draft a short-term dedicated commit (60 days) with pilot pricing. Well include options for autoscale and burst capacity.
[05:08] Maya: One more — compare quantized model quality vs baseline quantized variant. Baseline said theyre on int8.
[05:15] Priya: We matched a baseline int8 run; Redwood int8 + kernel tuning did slightly better, likely due to our kernel optimiser and caching behavior. We added side-by-side outputs in the sheet for your eval team.
[05:28] Alex: Recap: Priya will run the extended int8/int4 on 16k context and push results, Ill share SOC2 and KMS docs, Samir will try to provide traffic patterns, Jordan will confirm security stakeholders and Alex to draft pilot dedicated pricing.
[05:43] Jordan: Sounds good, thanks. Any blockers on your side?
[05:46] Priya: No blockers; just need the traffic sample and a green light to run int4 which wed recommend only as an exploratory test.
[05:55] Maya: OK give us the risk notes for int4.
[05:57] Priya: Will do — short note in the sheet (tab: quantization-risks).
[06:04] Alex: Alright if no more questions well wrap, sending notes and updated benchmarks by EOD tomorrow.
[06:10] Jordan: Thanks all.
[06:12] Speaker 2: (unlabeled) thanks; call ends.
